stem:
Nitya looks at the diagram of polygon $PQRS$ on square-grid paper. Sides $PQ$ and $QR$ run along the grid lines. Side $PS$ cuts diagonally across grid squares.

Which claim about the boundary length is correct?

options.text: Call the answer grid path only, with one shared length label for every side.
Count the diagonal side $PS$ as $1$ grid unit, the same as a straight grid side.
Measure the straight sides in grid units and treat diagonal side $PS$ as longer than one straight grid unit, then add those lengths.
Say that calling the diagonal longer is what creates polygon $PQRS$ on the grid.

teacher.key_rationale: Straight grid sides and a diagonal cut have different unit lengths, so the boundary must use separate straight and diagonal measures. One shared label, treating the diagonal as one straight unit, or reversing cause and effect miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source kite-on-grid as polygon PQRS with two straight grid sides and one diagonal side labelled.
